title: Take one ML project end to end
summary: A model trained on real data, evaluated honestly, served behind an API and documented with a model card: the project you talk through in every interview.
brief:
Interviewers ask about the project you know best. Build one you can defend in depth: a real dataset, a problem framed from a goal, a baseline, an evaluation you trust, a model served behind an API, and a model card that says where it fails.

Pick a public tabular, text or recommendation dataset with a clear prediction target and a time dimension if you can (churn, fraud, demand, click-through, ratings). Then work through it the way the ML system design framework does:

1. **Frame it.** The business goal, the ML task, the metric that stands in for the goal, and the latency and scale it would need.
2. **Baseline first.** A rule or a simple model, so every later number has something to beat.
3. **Features and model.** Leakage-free features (split by time where it matters), one stronger model, tuned with a validation set you never peek at.
4. **Evaluate honestly.** The offline metric with a confidence interval, a slice analysis (where does it fail?), and calibration if the scores feed a decision.
5. **Serve it.** A small HTTP API that loads the model artefact and validates input, with a test and a latency number.
6. **Document it.** A model card: intended use, data, metrics by slice, limitations, and what you would monitor after launch.

Then prepare the story: a five-minute walkthrough and answers to the follow-ups (why this metric, what leaks, what would you do with ten times the data).

milestones.title: Frame the problem and estimate scale
Evaluate a model honestly
milestones.note: If your project is not a recommender, take the method: time-based splits, full ranking, coverage and bias checks.

milestones.title: Tell it as a design interview

deliverables: A public repository with data loading, training, evaluation and the API, runnable from the README
A README that opens with the results table: baseline against final model, with confidence intervals and the main slices
A model card: intended use, data, metrics by slice, limitations and what you would monitor
A served API with an input-validation test and a measured p50 and p95 latency
A one-page design doc or a five-minute recorded walkthrough of the project as you would present it in an interview

rubric.meets: The goal, the ML task and the metric are stated, and the metric is justified.
rubric.strong: The doc names the proxy gap (what the metric misses) and sizes latency and throughput needs.

rubric.meets: A baseline, a held-out test set and a leakage-free split.
rubric.strong: Confidence intervals, slice analysis and calibration, with a clear statement of what the offline number does not tell you.

rubric.meets: The API serves the saved model and validates its input.
rubric.strong: Tests cover training, features and the API; the training run is reproducible from a pinned config.
The card includes failure examples and a monitoring plan with the signal, threshold and response for each risk.

rubric.meets: You can walk through the project in five minutes.
rubric.strong: You can answer the hard follow-ups: leakage, scale, what you would do next and why.

resume: Built an end-to-end [task] model on [dataset]: [metric] [x] (vs [y] baseline, 95% CI [a, b]), served via a validated API at [z] ms p95, with a model card and slice analysis.
